title: Supernatural (American TV series)
wiki_lead:
Supernatural is an American dark fantasy television series created by Eric Kripke that ran for 15 seasons. It premiered on The WB on September 13, 2005, moved to The CW in 2006, and ended on November 19, 2020. Starring Jared Padalecki and Jensen Ackles, the show follows brothers Sam and Dean Winchester, who hunt ghosts, monsters, and other supernatural beings. Throughout the series, they battle angels and demons while trying to save the world and prevent the Apocalypse. Guest actors Misha Collins, Mark A. Sheppard, and Mark Pellegrino were promoted to series regulars.
The project originated from Kripke's idea of a cross-country road trip and was approved by Warner Bros. It ran for four showrunner periods: Kripke (seasons 1–5), Sera Gamble (seasons 6–7), Jeremy Carver (seasons 8–11), and the duo of Andrew Dabb and Robert Singer (seasons 12–15). The writing is based on a monster-of-the-week concept and incorporates brotherly codependency, Americana, family psychology, Judeo-Christian mythology, and self-referential humor. Production was based in Vancouver, British Columbia, with chiaroscuro cinematography by Serge Ladouceur and an in-house visual effects department to save on costs. The soundtrack combines original music by Jay Gruska and Christopher Lennertz with classic rock songs, including "Carry On Wayward Son" by Kansas.
Most episodes had an audience of over a million viewers in the United States, peaking at 5.82 million. It was the longest-running series on The CW and the longest-running fantasy series in American television history. The complete 15-season series was released on DVD and Blu-ray on May 25, 2021. Critical reception of the show was mixed to positive; critics praised the on-screen chemistry of Padalecki and Ackles and called the first five seasons its peak. Other reviewers criticized the repetitive storylines and confusing plots of later seasons. Supernatural was nominated for three Primetime Emmy Awards and won nine People's Choice Awards. The series developed a large fan base that regularly attends conventions. Other media include novel and comic adaptations as well as spin-offs such as The Winchesters (2022–2023).

Plot

In their childhood, Sam and Dean Winchester lose their mother Mary to a mysterious supernatural creature, prompting their father John to raise them as hunters to track it. The first three seasons focus on the brothers' lives as hunters on the road, beginning with their search for their missing father. Sam is studying at Stanford University with his girlfriend Jessica until she is killed in the same way as his mother. He then leaves school and joins Dean; they travel around the United States hunting monsters, ghosts, demons, and other supernatural beings which are often drawn from folklore and urban legends.

grok_lead: Supernatural is an American dark fantasy drama television series created by Eric Kripke, starring Jared Padalecki as Sam Winchester and Jensen Ackles as Dean Winchester, two brothers who travel across the United States in a 1967 Chevrolet Impala, hunting demons, ghosts, monsters, and other supernatural entities while unraveling family secrets and apocalyptic threats. The series blends genres of horror, action-adventure, mystery, and drama, featuring a mix of standalone "monster-of-the-week" episodes and overarching mythological arcs involving angels, gods, and cosmic battles. Premiering on September 13, 2005, on The WB network, Supernatural transitioned to The CW after the networks' merger and ran for 15 seasons, totaling 327 episodes until its series finale on November 19, 2020. Originally envisioned by Kripke as a five-season story, the show's popularity led to its extension, evolving from episodic hunts to complex narratives exploring themes of family, destiny, and redemption. The series introduced recurring characters like the angel Castiel, played by Misha Collins, who joins the brothers in later seasons, adding layers to its supernatural lore. Produced by Warner Bros. Television, Supernatural developed a devoted fanbase, often called the "SPN Family," known for conventions and fan campaigns that contributed to its longevity. It received three Primetime Emmy Award nominations, including for Outstanding Sound Editing in 2006 and 2008, and Outstanding Music Composition in 2006, and earned two wins at the Saturn Awards, for Best Network Television Series in 2006 and Best Television Series in 2010.
